institution: Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, Srinagar
citation: Department of Microbiology, Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, Soura, Srinagar. Antibiogram 2024. Srinagar: SKIMS; 2025.
reporting: Percent susceptible by organism, specimen group (urine; blood; respiratory, sterile body fluids, pus and swabs combined) and location (IPD, OPD, ICU), with n per location; organism isolation tables by specimen and location.
method: Testing according to CLSI M100 (printed as "35th Ed CLSI supplement M100; 2024"); species with test data for fewer than 30 isolates generally excluded (as stated).

verification.note: All six susceptibility tables (pages 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11) parsed from the PDF text layer with pdfplumber (ruled table cells, colour markers kept to tell a black-marked 0 from a red 0), then every cell compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 2.2 and cropped into halves; the three organism tables (pages 3, 6, 9) read from the text layer and checked on the images (2026-09-26). A blind re-read of 6 random cells (value read from a crop of header and row before looking at the extracted value) found no differences.

notes: Specimen-wise antibiogram with each organism split by IPD (wards), OPD and ICU. The third specimen group is printed as "Respiratory/Sterile Body Fluids/Pus/Swab Samples" (the report's summary table calls the same group "Pus & Body Fluids", 2,658 clinically significant bacteria) and is recorded as pus, wounds and body fluids: it includes respiratory samples. Cells printed as "-", "IR" or a bare black or grey marker are left out; values printed as 0 are recorded as 0. In the Gram-negative urine table (page 5) the legend defines the black marker as "Not tested / IR"; its 35 black-marked zeros are therefore not measured percentages and are left out (listed in excluded), while its red-marked zeros are kept. The blood Gram-positive and respiratory/pus Gram-negative tables define the black marker as "0% or IR", and their black-marked zeros are recorded as 0. Enterococcus gentamicin columns are printed as GEN without saying high-level, and are recorded as gentamicin. The PDF's last three pages (15 to 17) are blank. Colour-coded efficacy bands differ between tables and are not recorded.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 798 cells of the six susceptibility tables (the seeded sample of 200 plus every other cell), all 76 row n with their IPD/OPD/ICU labels and all 117 organism-table counts re-read against the page images (scale 2.5 to 3.5, tables cropped into halves or bands), each value read before comparing; black-marked cells also confirmed in the PDF text layer. 0 transcription errors in values, n, settings, organisms or counts.

Removed on the lead's instruction: the 35 cells of the urine Gram-negative table (page 5) printed as 0 with the black marker, which that table's legend defines as "Not tested / IR" (33 were flagged caution and 2, Pseudomonas ICU ceftriaxone and Acinetobacter ICU ertapenem, intrinsic; all 35 carried the same conflict entry, removed with them). Each was checked on the page image and in the text layer; they are listed once in excluded. The red-marked 0 in that table (Proteus IPD tobramycin) is kept, and the 9 black-marked zeros of the blood Gram-positive table and the 21 of the respiratory/pus Gram-negative table stay as 0, since those legends read "0% or IR".

Cells not kept by the rules, re-read and printed as recorded: Enterococcus GEN in urine (51.02, 76.9, 0), blood (10, 28) and respiratory/pus (78.3, 70, 50), intrinsic because the column is printed as GEN without 'high-level' (the page 12 overall chart labels the Enterococcus agent GEN-HL); Pseudomonas urine ceftriaxone 59 and 74 and respiratory/pus ampicillin-sulbactam 18, 19.6 and 0; Acinetobacter urine ertapenem 50 and 11 and fosfomycin 48, 42 and 20; Enterobacter blood amoxicillin-clavulanate 13, 0 and 0; MRSA blood IPD and OPD penicillin 20 and ampicillin 25 (suppressed).

Cautions re-read and printed as recorded: urine Enterococcus ICU nitrofurantoin 60 (n=4); blood Pseudomonas IPD gentamicin 5, ceftazidime 7, aztreonam 5 (n=11); blood Salmonella ICU aztreonam 80 (n=4); respiratory/pus CoNS OPD 16, 92, 85, 40 (n=3) and ICU 14, 85, 82, 22 (n=2); Enterococcus IPD ampicillin 62.8, vancomycin 92.5, linezolid 98 (n=21) and OPD penicillin 47, vancomycin 95.2, teicoplanin 95 (n=11); Proteus IPD ertapenem 75.2, OPD cefepime 26.2, ICU ertapenem 75; Pseudomonas ICU gentamicin 54, piperacillin-tazobactam 50.8, ciprofloxacin 30, levofloxacin 30 (n=9); E. coli imipenem and meropenem 43.4 and 75.8 (IPD), 45 and 75 (OPD), 40 and 70 (ICU).

Count mismatch confirmed as printed: the urine Gram-negative table heads Acinetobacter spp. (47) but prints IPD (133) and OPD (19), while the urine organism table on page 3 gives 33 IPD, 9 OPD and 5 ICU (total 47). n kept as printed with the row notes; the derived urine all-settings Acinetobacter row therefore sums to 157, not 47.

Also confirmed: pages 9, 10 and 11 head the third specimen group "Respiratory/Sterile Body Fluids/Pus/Swab Samples" (filed as pus with that specimen_as_printed); the institution reads "Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, Srinagar".

Lead 2026-09-26: the "Respiratory/Sterile Body Fluids/Pus/Swab Samples" group (all specimens other than blood and urine) is filed under specimen "other" (not blood or urine), not pus; 26 rows and 39 counts moved.
